newsitem.title: USA: Triarc says Snapple buy made unit IPO moot.
newsitem.headline: Triarc says Snapple buy made unit IPO moot.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc said on Thursday that it chose not to proceed with its partial initial public offering because its purchase of Snapple Beverage Corp accomplished the same objective, repositioning Triarc as primarily a beverage company.
"Last October we were a holding company with some beverage operations," Triarc spokesman Martin Shea said in an interview. "Today we're a beverage company, with propane and some other assets."
After the announcement, Triarc shares closed up 5/8 to 22-3/4, a new year high.
Triarc in October 1996 announced plans for a partial initial public offering of its food and beverage businesses. Then in March it agreed to buy Snapple from Quaker Oats Co for $300 million in cash.
At that point, Standard & Poor's said it decided to leave some Triarc unit debt ratings on Creditwatch, where they had been placed after Triarc announced its planned offering.

Standard & Poor's said on April 1 that the CreditWatch listing reflected uncertainty as to the amount and future application of the proceeds from the offering, or to how the new consumer products company would be capitalized.
More recently, Oppenheimer & Co on May 6 downgraded Triarc to market perform from outperform.
On Thursday, the company said it completed the Snapple purchase and abandoned its plans for the offering.
Shea said Snapple's 1996 sales were $550 million, while Triarc's Mistic and Royal Crown beverage businesses together totalled $310 million.
Adding Snapple "just changes the dynamic," he said.
Besides its beverage and Arby's restaurant businesses, Triarc has annual sales of $71 million in specialty dyes and chemicals, and an equity interest in liquefied petroleum gas.
